items.title: Microsoft ships secure code sandboxes
items.oneliner: Run untrusted code on Windows, Linux, or macOS with VM, container, and process isolation from one SDK.

items.title: DuckDB gets a lakehouse format
items.oneliner: Open table format adds schema evolution, time travel, and change feeds using DuckDB plus Parquet.

items.title: Python 3.15 is ready today
items.oneliner: Install the latest Python with UTF-8 default encoding, frozendict, JIT improvements, and a large standard library update.

items.title: Jujutsu improves Git-compatible workflows
items.oneliner: Git-compatible VCS adds colocated workspaces, multi-remote push, and cross-revision file edits without touching your working copy.

items.title: Cache expensive CLI commands locally
items.oneliner: Small daemon caches command output with TTLs and tenant keys, cutting repeated auth and slow shell workflows.

items.title: Agents can point at your screen
items.oneliner: macOS CLI draws arrows, boxes, and text overlays so AI agents can guide users through permission prompts.

items.title: Reverse engineering toolkit in one repo
items.oneliner: Large GitHub toolkit bundles Binwalk, pwntools, and workflows for analyzing binaries, firmware, and runtime behavior.

items.title: Guix extensions now have a guide
items.oneliner: Hands-on tutorial shows how to add custom guix commands, package them, and expose help text cleanly.

items.title: RwLock benchmark shows hidden costs
items.oneliner: Practical Rust benchmark explains when read-heavy workloads lose to lock-free designs and how to measure it yourself.

items.title: Vectorized bit tricks for zero counts
items.oneliner: Deep optimization walkthrough shows faster CLZ and CTZ using SIMD-style floating-point tricks on modern CPUs.
